item.title: The Blue Wave Has Tech Bros Scrambling for Data Centers in Space
item.description: After Democrats won big in Texas and other AI infrastructure hot spots on Tuesday, data center enthusiasts looked for comfort in low Earth orbit.

item.title: The Biggest Pro-AI Super PAC Network Didn’t Really Impact the Midterms
item.description: Leading the Future, backed by Silicon Valley’s biggest billionaires, had a war chest of $100 million and an aggressive stance against AI regulation. All of it didn’t add up to much on Tuesday night.

item.title: Google Is Forcing AI Overviews in Classrooms. Schools Are Searching for a Way Out
item.description: Google is tying up AI Overviews with traditional search, angering parents and educators who worry that easy, machine-generated answers are leaving kids less capable.

item.title: Hugging Face’s CEO Says His P(Doom) Is ‘Close to Zero’
item.description: “Most of the risk is actually created by a couple of players building behind closed doors,” Clément Delangue said of the need for open source AI.

item.title: The Results Are In: Voters Hate Data Centers
item.description: From high-profile Senate races to local rezoning initiatives, data centers and their supporters did miserably on the ballot in the 2026 midterms.

item.title: UK Officials Said AI Would Add £400 Billion to the Economy. That Figure Mainly Came From Google
item.description: The AI minister now concedes the estimated figure is less than a third of that. Researchers blame the country’s slow rate of adoption.

item.title: Here’s Why You Shouldn’t Use AI to Vote
item.description: From hallucinations to partisan bias, artificial intelligence chatbots like ChatGPT and Claude are not helpful when it comes to Election Day.

item.title: ‘Our Risk, Their Reward’: Zohran Mamdani on AI and Data Centers
item.description: Ahead of the midterms, WIRED talked to New York City’s mayor about data centers, AI in schools, and the future of the Democratic party.

item.title: When You Should—and Shouldn’t—Use AI to Search the Web
item.description: Chatbots are often quite good at retrieving the information you want from the web. But sometimes you’ll get better results by typing your query into a good old search engine.

item.title: Hundreds of Mundane AI Apps Are Hiding Sexually Abusive Deepfake Features
item.description: WIRED uncovered some 400 apps and websites linked to Chinese-language developers that look like regular AI tools but had secret features that let users create violent AI-generated images and video.
